# diagnosticSummary <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" width="100" height="100" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/overdodactyl/diagnosticSummary/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/overdodactyl/diagnosticSummary/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`diagnosticSummary` summarizes how well predicted probabilities agree with a binary reference standard. One call to `dx()` gives:

- sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, the AUC, and other measures, with confidence intervals
- the same measures at other thresholds and by subgroup
- plots such as ROC, precision-recall, calibration, and decision curves, and a forest plot of subgroups (`dx_plot_*()`)

`dx_compare()` compares models, and `dx_itd()` handles missing predictions.

## Installation

You can install the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("overdodactyl/diagnosticSummary")
```
## Example


```{r example}
library(diagnosticSummary)
# Load sample data
data("dx_heart_failure")
head(dx_heart_failure)

# Create dx object
dx_obj <- dx(
  data = dx_heart_failure,
  true_varname = "truth",
  pred_varname = "predicted",
  threshold_range = c(.1,.2,.3),
  setthreshold = .3,
  doboot = TRUE,
  bootreps = 1000,
  grouping_variables = c("AgeGroup", "Sex", "AgeSex")
)
```

Printing the object gives a short overview:

```{r print}
dx_obj
```

`summary()` shows every measure, and `as.data.frame()` returns them with unformatted estimates and confidence limits:

```{r summary}
summary(dx_obj, variable = "Overall", show_var = FALSE, show_label = FALSE)
```

## Plots

```{r roc, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6, out.width = "60%", dpi = 150}
dx_plot_roc(dx_obj)
```

## Comparing models

```{r compare}
dx_rf <- dx(
  data = dx_heart_failure,
  true_varname = "truth",
  pred_varname = "predicted_rf",
  setthreshold = .3
)

dx_compare(list(Logistic = dx_obj, `Random forest` = dx_rf), paired = TRUE)
```


## Missing predictions

If some predictions are missing, for example because a case failed quality control, `dx_itd()` keeps those cases as ungradable results in a 3x2 intention-to-diagnose analysis. It reports the diagnostic yield, post-test disease risks and likelihood ratios for each result, and worst-case performance, which counts every ungradable result as incorrect.

```{r itd}
data_missing <- dx_heart_failure
data_missing$predicted[seq(5, 261, by = 20)] <- NA

itd_obj <- dx_itd(
  data = data_missing,
  true_varname = "truth",
  pred_varname = "predicted",
  setthreshold = .3
)

dx_itd_table(itd_obj)
```
